paragraphs.source_en: At dusk on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month of Tenshō 10, Oda Nobunaga arrived at Honnō-ji accompanied only by the Mori Ranmaru brothers and some fifty other personal guards.

units.source_en: At dusk on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month of Tenshō 10, Oda Nobunaga arrived at Honnō-ji accompanied only by the Mori Ranmaru brothers and some fifty other personal guards.
units.source_zh: 天正十年五月二十九的黄昏时分，织田信长只带了森兰丸兄弟等五十多名贴身侍卫，来到本能寺。

paragraphs.source_zh: 天正十年五月二十九的黄昏时分，织田信长只带了森兰丸兄弟等五十多名贴身侍卫，来到本能寺。

paragraphs.source_en: The women and more than two hundred guards had arrived well before him, but rain began falling that afternoon, and they anxiously awaited Nobunaga while cursing the wretched weather.

units.source_en: The women and more than two hundred guards had arrived well before him, but rain began falling that afternoon, and they anxiously awaited Nobunaga while cursing the wretched weather.

paragraphs.source_zh: 女人们以及二百多名护卫早已抵达此处，可是，下午时分，天上却下起雨来，人们一边诅咒着鬼天气，一边焦急地等候信长的到来。

paragraphs.source_en: Whenever Nobunaga entered the capital, the nobles and high officials would invariably go out to Yamashina early to receive him, smothering him in elaborate, insincere courtesies. Nobunaga had always detested such hollow formalities.

paragraphs.source_en: He had probably been detained once again by all that ceremony, and could scarcely have avoided getting soaked. The thought made Lady Nō restless as she directed the women in cleaning and preparing Honnō-ji, where she had arrived a day earlier.

paragraphs.source_en: His eldest son Nobutada, a lieutenant general of the third rank, had escorted Ieyasu to Myōkaku-ji, then entrusted Hasegawa Takemaru and Sugihara Shichirōzaemon with conducting him from Osaka into the port of Sakai. Nobutada had subsequently moved to Nijō Castle, leaving only his young brother Genzaburō Katsunaga at Myōkaku-ji. Sankurō Nobutaka had dispatched troops to Sumiyoshi and was preparing to cross the sea and attack Awa. Thus, the Oda brothers had swiftly completed their dispositions for the campaign in the Chūgoku region and now waited only for their father Nobunaga to enter the capital.

paragraphs.source_en: Nobunaga had therefore intended to avoid every possible formality so that father and sons might hasten to the battlefield. But upon reaching the capital, he found matters far less simple than he had imagined. Every court noble and minister feared Nobunaga, and so they repeated their hollow courtesies endlessly and vied to ingratiate themselves with him. No sooner had he dismissed one with a few curt words than another, still more tedious, appeared.
